atoms.name: Linear search cost
atoms.one_line: Absent key costs n comparisons; present key costs (n+1)/2 on average.

atoms.name: Binary search mechanics
atoms.one_line: Needs sorted data and random access; each probe halves the range, T(n)=T(n/2)+1.

atoms.name: Counting comparisons exactly
atoms.one_line: Worst case is floor(log2 n)+1 probes, found or not; watch the cost per probe.

atoms.name: Preconditions, duplicates, bugs
atoms.one_line: Linked lists lose the speedup; equal keys need a lower-bound variant; lo=mid can loop forever.

atoms.name: Search in structured arrays
atoms.one_line: Rotated, bitonic, 0/1 and row-column sorted inputs still allow log n or m+n probes.

atoms.name: Lower bounds and adversaries
atoms.one_line: Outcome counting gives ceil(log2(n+1)); unsorted search needs n-1 comparisons to find the maximum.
